q: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body or mind that leads to poor _____.
e: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body or mind that leads to poor health. So we write health. Leave diet and growth out.

q: Non-infectious diseases are caused by factors such as aging, genetics, malnutrition, lifestyle and _____.
e: Non-infectious diseases are caused by factors such as aging, genetics, malnutrition, lifestyle and environment. Environment is the word, not bacteria or viruses.

q: Most cardiovascular disease starts with _____ formation.
e: Most cardiovascular disease starts with atheroma formation. Atheroma is the word, not plaque or thrombus.

q: The inner lining of the wall of the artery is called the _____.
e: The inner lining of the wall of the artery is called the endothelium. The blank is endothelium. Not lumen or plaque.

q: White blood cells and lipids clump together under the endothelium to form fatty _____.
e: White blood cells and lipids clump together under the endothelium to form fatty streaks. The blank is streaks. Not plaques or clots.

q: The hardening of arteries, caused by atheroma, is called _____.
e: The hardening of arteries, caused by atheroma, is called atherosclerosis. So we write atherosclerosis. Leave thrombosis and angina out.

q: In angina, plaques build up slowly in the _____ arteries.
e: In angina, plaques build up slowly in the coronary arteries. Coronary is the word, not pulmonary or carotid.

q: The narrowed coronary arteries cannot supply enough oxygenated blood and the heart muscle resorts to _____ respiration.
e: The narrowed coronary arteries cannot supply enough oxygenated blood and the heart muscle resorts to anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic is the word, not aerobic or cellular.

q: Myocardial infarction is more commonly known as a heart _____.
e: Myocardial infarction is more commonly known as a heart attack. Attack is the word, not failure or blockage.

q: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the _____.
e: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the brain. The blank is brain. Not heart or lungs.

q: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is the formation of a blood clot in a vein deep inside the body, usually in _____ veins.
e: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is the formation of a blood clot in a vein deep inside the body, usually in leg veins. The blank is leg. Not arm or neck.

q: There are _____ main non-modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
e: There are three main non-modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease. So we write three. Leave two and four out.

q: Men are more likely to suffer from heart disease than women, making _____ a non-modifiable risk factor.
e: Men are more likely to suffer from heart disease than women, making gender a non-modifiable risk factor. So we write gender. Leave age and genetics out.

q: A healthy blood pressure is around _____ mmHg during systole.
e: A healthy blood pressure is around 120 mmHg during systole. So we write 120. Leave 80 and 140 out.

q: A healthy blood pressure is around 80 mmHg during _____.
e: A healthy blood pressure is around 80 mmHg during diastole. Diastole is the word, not systole or pulse.

q: If the blood pressure is regularly above _____ mmHg, it is a sign of high blood pressure.
e: If the blood pressure is regularly above 140/90 mmHg, it is a sign of high blood pressure. 140/90 is the word, not 120/80 or 130/85.

q: An ideal body mass index (BMI) range is 18.5 to _____ $kg/m^2$.
e: An ideal body mass index (BMI) range is 18.5 to 25 kg/m squared. So we write 25. Leave 30 and 20 out.

q: Beta blockers and ACE inhibitors are examples of _____ drugs.
e: Beta blockers and ACE inhibitors are examples of antihypertensives drugs. The blank is antihypertensives. Not statins or anticoagulants.

q: A group of drugs known as _____ is used to lower the level of cholesterol in the blood.
e: A group of drugs known as statins is used to lower the level of cholesterol in the blood. Statins is the word, not antibiotics or diuretics.

q: Warfarin and heparin are examples of _____ medicines used to reduce blood clotting.
e: Warfarin and heparin are examples of anticoagulants medicines used to reduce blood clotting. So we write anticoagulants. Leave painkillers and beta blockers out.

q: Aspirin is a type of platelet _____ drug.
e: Aspirin is a type of platelet inhibitory drug. Inhibitory is the word, not stimulating or producing.

q: Infectious diseases are sometimes called _____ diseases as they are passed from infected to uninfected people.
e: Infectious diseases are sometimes called communicable diseases as they are passed from infected to uninfected people. The blank is communicable. Not endemic or chronic.

q: Diseases that are always in populations are described as _____.
e: Diseases that are always in populations are described as endemic. Endemic is the word, not epidemic or pandemic.

q: An _____ occurs when there is a sudden increase in the number of people with a disease.
e: An epidemic occurs when there is a sudden increase in the number of people with a disease. Epidemic is the word, not endemic or outbreak.

q: A _____ occurs when there is an increase in the number of cases throughout a continent or across the world.
e: A pandemic occurs when there is an increase in the number of cases throughout a continent or across the world. So we write pandemic. Leave epidemic and plague out.

q: The death rate from different diseases is referred to as _____.
e: The death rate from different diseases is referred to as mortality. So we write mortality. Leave morbidity and prevalence out.

q: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio _____.
e: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. Cholerae is the word, not tuberculosis or parahaemolyticus.

q: Malaria is caused by four species of the protist _____.
e: Malaria is caused by four species of the protist plasmodium. The blank is plasmodium. Not amoeba or paramecium.

q: HIV/AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency _____.
e: HIV/AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency virus. Virus is the word, not bacterium or protist.

q: Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and M. _____.
e: Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and M. bovis. Bovis is the word, not leprae or avium.

q: The insect vector for malaria is the female _____ mosquito.
e: The insect vector for malaria is the female anopheles mosquito. The blank is anopheles. Not aedes or culex.

q: The incubation period for malaria is from a week to a _____.
e: The incubation period for malaria is from a week to a year. Year is the word, not month or day.

q: The site of action of the malaria pathogen includes the liver, red blood cells, and _____.
e: The site of action of the malaria pathogen includes the liver, red blood cells, and brain. So we write brain. Leave lungs and kidneys out.

q: Microscopical examination of blood and dip stick tests are methods of _____ for malaria.
e: Microscopical examination of blood and dip stick tests are methods of diagnosis for malaria. So we write diagnosis. Leave treatment and prevention out.

q: In 2012, about _____ percent of malaria cases worldwide were in Africa.
e: In 2012, about 80 percent of malaria cases worldwide were in Africa. 80 is the word, not 50 or 90.

q: In 2012, about 90 percent of malaria mortality worldwide occurred in _____.
e: In 2012, about 90 percent of malaria mortality worldwide occurred in africa. The blank is africa. Not asia or South America.

q: Male and female gametes of Plasmodium fuse in the mosquito's _____.
e: Male and female gametes of Plasmodium fuse in the mosquito's gut. The blank is gut. Not salivary glands or blood.

q: The infective stages of malaria pass from the mosquito's salivary glands into the human's blood together with the _____.
e: The infective stages of malaria pass from the mosquito's salivary glands into the human's blood together with the anticoagulant. The blank is anticoagulant. Not venom or enzymes.

q: Malaria may also be transmitted during blood transfusion and when unsterile _____ are re-used.
e: Malaria may also be transmitted during blood transfusion and when unsterile needles are re-used. Needles is the word, not syringes or scalpels.

q: Quinine and chloroquine are anti-malarial drugs used as _____ drugs to prevent infection.
e: Quinine and chloroquine are anti-malarial drugs used as prophylactic drugs to prevent infection. The blank is prophylactic. Not painkiller or antibiotic.

q: Chloroquine inhibits protein synthesis and prevents the parasite spreading within the _____.
e: Chloroquine inhibits protein synthesis and prevents the parasite spreading within the body. The blank is body. Not mosquito or liver.

q: Proguanil inhibits the sexual reproduction of Plasmodium inside the biting _____.
e: Proguanil inhibits the sexual reproduction of Plasmodium inside the biting mosquito. Mosquito is the word, not human or larva.

q: Mefloquine is a drug used in South America, Africa and New _____.
e: Mefloquine is a drug used in South America, Africa and New guinea. The blank is guinea. Not zealand or caledonia.

q: Artesunate is derived from the plant compound _____.
e: Artesunate is derived from the plant compound artemisinin. Artemisinin is the word, not quinine or nicotine.

q: Mosquito larvae and pupae can be suffocated by spreading _____ over the surfaces of water.
e: Mosquito larvae and pupae can be suffocated by spreading oil over the surfaces of water. So we write oil. Leave salt and chlorine out.

q: Mosquito fish, scientifically known as Gambusia _____, feed on mosquito larvae.
e: Mosquito fish, scientifically known as Gambusia affinis, feed on mosquito larvae. The blank is affinis. Not mosquitofish or aquatica.

q: The bacterium Bacillus _____ kills mosquito larvae but is not toxic to other forms of life.
e: The bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis kills mosquito larvae but is not toxic to other forms of life. So we write thuringiensis. Leave subtilis and anthracis out.

q: Soaking mosquito nets in insecticide every _____ months has been shown to reduce mortality from malaria.
e: Soaking mosquito nets in insecticide every six months has been shown to reduce mortality from malaria. The blank is six. Not three or twelve.

q: In the 1950s, the World Health Organization coordinated a worldwide malaria _____ programme.
e: In the 1950s, the World Health Organization coordinated a worldwide malaria eradication programme. Eradication is the word, not control or vaccination.

q: Mosquitoes became resistant to DDT and other insecticides such as _____.
e: Mosquitoes became resistant to DDT and other insecticides such as dieldrin. So we write dieldrin. Leave malathion and permethrin out.

q: Between 2000 and 2011, control measures achieved a decrease in malaria mortality rates of about 25% across the world, and _____% in the WHO's African region.
e: Between 2000 and 2011, control measures achieved a decrease in malaria mortality rates of about 25% across the world, and 33% in the WHO's African region. 33 is the word, not 20 or 50.

q: About _____ percent of the world's population lives in areas where there is a risk of malaria.
e: About 40 percent of the world's population lives in areas where there is a risk of malaria. 40 is the word, not 20 or 60.

q: The whole genome of Plasmodium has been sequenced, which may lead to the development of effective _____.
e: The whole genome of Plasmodium has been sequenced, which may lead to the development of effective vaccines. So we write vaccines. Leave antibiotics and insecticides out.

q: Deep vein thrombosis risk is increased by prolonged _____ such as during long-haul flights.
e: Deep vein thrombosis risk is increased by prolonged inactivity such as during long-haul flights. The blank is inactivity. Not sleeping or eating.

q: A stroke blockage is usually caused by a blood clot, an atheroma or a combination of the _____.
e: A stroke blockage is usually caused by a blood clot, an atheroma or a combination of the two. Two is the word, not three or four.
